title: Three scenes and a sleeping dog
summary: A Mini-Cast about one day of building animated scenes for the site: a canyon rescue, a deep sea and a workshop at night, and how each idea led to the next.

post.title: Three scenes and a sleeping dog
post.body:
It started with a missing link preview. My site didn't have a picture to show when someone shared it, so I went looking for one and found an old illustration of Marley and me at the edge of a canyon, her teeth in my hood, me hanging over the drop.

I wanted it to move, so I rebuilt it in layers: generate the pieces with AI image tools, then cut, place and animate every one by hand in code. My first try had Marley lying down, and it looked like she was chewing on me. She needed to be standing. She's saving me.

That logo made the Parts Catalog look bare, so it got a deep sea: Marley asleep in a glowing jellyfish, me as a diver holding out a cube of parts, plankton, an anglerfish with a flickering lure and, now and then, a giant paper squid passing through the dark.

Then the Workshop got a bench at night. The first version had me holding a soldering iron right over the sleeping dog. That had to go. Now I shape a hologram with my hands, a few of the site's paper animals stand on glowing discs, and Marley sleeps at the end of the bench with a little line of z's so nobody worries.

What I learned: subtle means a few percent of movement over several seconds, the pose carries the story, and a sleeping dog needs to visibly breathe.

episode.title: Three scenes and a sleeping dog
episode.script:
This one started with a small, practical problem. Christian wanted his website to look right when someone shared a link. Every site has a little picture for that. His didn't.

***

So he went looking for one, and he found a gem. An old illustration of himself and Marley at the edge of a canyon. Marley has the top of his hood in her mouth, and Christian is hanging out over the drop. It is, in its way, a rescue. A very good dog doing a very good job.

The plan was to turn that picture into a little animation for the corner of the site, rebuilt in layers so the pieces could move.

The first try wasn't quite right. With Marley lying down, it looked less like a rescue and more like a dog having her dinner. Christian put it perfectly. She needs to be standing. She is saving me. He was right. Seeing what a picture is really saying is the whole job.

***

They kept the portrait close in, her chin on his hood. He sinks a little. His eyes go wide. She eases him back up, and his eyes relax. Not sleepy. Relaxed. That took a few tries, and the patience shows. It's the difference between cute and charming.

Then the seasons came in. Blossoms in spring. Snow falling in winter. A moon and stars at night. The autumn leaves were too much, so they went. Now that tiny picture in the corner changes with the sky above the lake.

***

One great logo made the next page look bare. The Parts Catalog, a whole library of every animal and tree the site can draw, still had a plain little dot.

So Christian brought in a new picture. Deep water. Marley curled up asleep inside a glowing jellyfish. And Christian in an old brass diving helmet, holding out a small glowing cube of parts.

This time the pieces came separately. The diver. The dog. The jellyfish. The water. Then a handful of small sea creatures, each with its own soft light inside. An anglerfish got a lamp on its lure that flickers on every so often. The smallest creatures became plankton, and a few drift right past in front, out of focus, the way things do underwater.

Even the title got a drop of water in it. Two shades of blue, borrowed straight from inside the jellyfish.

And far below, every so often, something very large passes by. A giant paper squid, low in the dark, mostly shadow. Only its eye glows.

***

Then, the workshop. A page for building new parts deserved a place where things actually get built.

Old school or new? Both. A worn wooden bench, a brass lamp, pegboards full of tools. And one thing from the future. A hologram.

In the first version, Christian was holding a soldering iron, with Marley asleep on the bench right in front of him. It looked, in his own words, like he was soldering the dog. So the iron went. Now he wears goggles and shapes a glowing blue hologram with his hands. An eagle. Then an owl. Then a hawk.

His hair came out too red at first. It's sandy, not ginger, and that difference matters. Fixed.

Along the bench, a few of the site's own paper animals stand on little glowing discs. A doe. A mule deer buck. A black bear. And an elk bull, because, as Christian pointed out, an elk bull is massive. They all face him now, not the dog.

***

There was one last touch. Marley, stretched out and very still at the end of the bench, could be read the wrong way.

So she got a slow, visible breath, and a little line of z's drifting up from her head.

She's asleep. She's fine. And she is, as always, the best part of the picture.
